title: Dominic and the Scholarship
premise: Marguerite Eriksen has perfected invisibility—until a group chat called The Scholarship begins posting predictions that come true, each one naming her family. The chat was built by Dominic Vale, the withdrawn son of the late billionaire whose will funds both the school's academic scholarship and its championship legacy; his algorithm mines student data to forecast who will 'deserve' the money, and the Eriksens are next on the list. As Marguerite races through a meaningless quiz-bowl championship to reach the real prize—the final audition for the Vale Scholarship—she must decide whether exposing Dominic's corrupted system is worth destroying the only friendship that ever saw her. She wins the audition, exposes the machine, and chooses truth over the inheritance, keeping loyalty to her siblings instead.
about_author: Silas Sterling is the pen name of a former debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers trade integrity for advantage. They write in a drafty attic office, fueled by black coffee and stories about kids the world underestimated.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A day in her carefully managed invisibility: packing lunches, covering for her brother Theo's detention, acing a chemistry quiz no one notices. Establishes the weight she carries and the armor of anonymity. Emotional beat: competent exhaustion, pride disguised as silence.

chapters.title: The First Prediction
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. An unknown group chat adds her with a single message: 'Eriksen. Water main. Tuesday.' Tuesday, the gym floods. She tells no one, but the coincidence burrows under her skin. Emotional beat: unease dressed up as rationality.

chapters.title: Second Sight, Third Sibling
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The chat predicts her sister Junie's lost recital solo—and it happens exactly as posted. Mom works a double; Marguerite holds the household together alone. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Dominic Vale, Ghost of the West Wing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She tracks the chat's metadata to the library carrel where Dominic Vale sits—son of the dead billionaire whose name is on half the school. He neither confirms nor denies. Emotional beat: wary curiosity, two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Algorithm of Deserving
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We see the machine he inherited from his father's notes: a model that scores students' futures and posts predictions to shape them. He believes he's running an experiment in merit. Emotional beat: righteous certainty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Quiz Bowl Tryouts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Coach Okafor pushes her toward the quiz-bowl team—the championship that 'doesn't matter' but feeds the Vale scoring system. She joins only to stay inside the machine's blind spot. Emotional beat: reluctant ambition.

chapters.title: What the Chat Promised Theo
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A new prediction targets Theo: 'Expelled by spring break.' Marguerite realizes the chat doesn't just foresee events—it engineers them. Emotional beat: protective fury.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic offers Marguerite a deal: help him validate the model, and the algorithm reroutes Theo's trajectory. She signs nothing but agrees to everything. Emotional beat: bargain struck in bad faith by both sides.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Quiz bowl regionals; Marguerite carries the team while scanning the crowd for whoever executes the predictions. She spots the school's development officer feeding data to Dominic. Emotional beat: the game behind the game revealed.

chapters.title: Junie Finds Out
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie discovers the chat has been predicting—and steering—her own life, including the solo she 'lost.' She confronts Marguerite about secrets kept 'for her own good.' Emotional beat: sisterhood strained by protection.

chapters.title: The Will
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She pulls the elder Vale's will from public records: the scholarship requires a 'demonstrably transformed recipient,' which explains why the machine manufactures crises first. Emotional beat: horror at the architecture of generosity.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Dominic's alternating POV. In the school archive they argue over whether prediction is prophecy or puppetry. For one night, honesty almost wins. Emotional beat: intimacy built on shared complicity.

chapters.title: Theo's Hearing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The engineered expulsion hearing arrives early. Marguerite uses what she's learned from the archive to dismantle the evidence—but spends a favor she can't afford. Emotional beat: victory with a bill attached.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Sabotage
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Someone leaks the team's prep materials; suspicion falls on Marguerite. The chat posts a new line: 'Eriksen falls before the final audition.' Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Development Officer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She uncovers years of manipulated scholarships—recipients chosen, broken, and remade to fit the will's language. Some winners never recovered. Emotional beat: dread deepening into moral clarity.

chapters.title: Dominic's Confession
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic admits he let the machine run because stopping it means admitting his father's legacy is rot—and losing the only version of himself anyone respects. Emotional beat: self-loathing seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Dominic offers her the ultimate deal: win the final audition quietly, take the scholarship, and let the machine keep operating for other families. Her siblings need the money. Emotional beat: temptation at full strength.

chapters.title: Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The state quiz-bowl final. Marguerite plays brilliantly and deliberately loses the last match, refusing to feed the algorithm another data point. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Marguerite publishes the ledger, the will's clause, and the chat's logs. The school convulses; the development officer resigns; families demand answers. Emotional beat: catharsis with collateral damage.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Vale Scholarship audition proceeds amid scandal. Asked what she'd do with power, Marguerite answers with the truth about the machine—including Dominic's role. Emotional beat: integrity tested on stage.

chapters.title: What She Refused
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She wins the scholarship and declines it publicly, redirecting attention to every family the system broke. Dominic, facing consequences, finally deletes the chat. Emotional beat: grief and freedom entangled.

chapters.title: Head Up, Locker Open
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Spring: mom takes days shifts, Theo thrives, Junie sings her solo again. Dominic leaves a paper letter—no algorithms—apologizing without asking forgiveness. Marguerite walks the halls visible, unafraid. Emotional beat: earned peace.
